title: Vectorized Revenue Calculation
prompt: Given units = np.array([3, 10, 5]) and prices = np.array([24.5, 4.25, 18.0]), compute total_revenue (float) using vectorized multiplication and .sum() without any Python loop.
hints: Call .sum() on the product and wrap in float().
solution:
import numpy as np
units = np.array([3, 10, 5])
prices = np.array([24.5, 4.25, 18.0])
total_revenue = float((units * prices).sum())
explanation: Element-wise multiplication followed by .sum() computes the dot product cleanly.

title: Boolean Masking With &
prompt: Fill in the blanks to filter values strictly between 10 and 50 in NumPy.
solution:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([5, 20, 45, 60])
filtered = a[(a > 10) & (a < 50)]
explanation: NumPy boolean masks combine conditions with & and | inside parentheses.

title: NumPy axis=0 vs axis=1
prompt: Recall what axis=0 and axis=1 aggregate along.
solution: axis=0 aggregates down rows (one result per column); axis=1 aggregates across columns (one result per row).
front: In a 2D NumPy array, what does `arr.mean(axis=0)` compute vs `arr.mean(axis=1)`?
back: `axis=0` computes the mean down rows (per column); `axis=1` computes the mean across columns (per row).

title: NumPy boolean operators
prompt: Recall element-wise logical operators in NumPy.
front: Which operators combine boolean conditions on NumPy arrays?
back: `&` (and), `|` (or), and `~` (not), with parentheses around each comparison.
